disposition_reason: The source tests a causal perturbation effect on behavior and EEG. Increasing an effect or its significance does not improve a prediction or estimator against known truth. Existing fixed-region and behavioral scorers reproduce specified summaries; selecting different windows or exclusions cannot become a same-task paper victory.

source_paper.title: Perturbing human V1 degrades the fidelity of visual working memory

evidence.locator: Figure 2A-C and Methods: behavioral analysis and EEG
evidence.supports: Paired TMS/no-TMS effects with 15 participants; uncertainty tests biological contrasts.
Figure 2B uses released masterTFR derivative, specified time/frequency windows and subject averaging.
Historical reconstruction, participant-position limits and 15-versus16 source discrepancy are not improvement evidence.

target.description: TMS effects on spatial memory error, alpha lateralization and occipital alpha/beta responses.

dataset.description: Released experiment derivatives used by the author Figure 2B route: masterTFR_allsubs.mat; behavioral analysis uses the source memory task.

cohort.description: Figure 2 reports 15 paired participants. Released arrays contain 15 positions, but exact physical-person-to-position identity is not verified; the sample count alone does not authenticate the original cohort join.

split.description: Within-person TMS/no-TMS and phosphene-field conditions, not a model train/test partition.

inputs.description: Condition-specific EEG power derivatives and memory-guided behavioral responses.

preprocessing.description: The reviewed Figure 2B script selects 0.5-2 and 3-4.5 seconds and 7-20Hz by strict bounds before plotting; this derivative route cannot vary raw artifact removal.

metric.description: Paired behavioral-error and physiological contrasts; a larger contrast or smaller cluster p-value is not an accuracy score.

aggregation.description: Participant summaries and paired contrasts; the figure script also averages subjects for the topographic display.

comparison.primary_metric: No ordered model-performance metric for the source perturbation effects

published_baseline.description: Reported behavioral and EEG effects are biological findings, not a model score to exceed.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: Existing source-compatible numerical summaries are calibration references.

minimum_effect.rationale: Neither stronger TMS effects nor outcome-selected windows define better scientific performance.

uncertainty.method: Preserve paired-person uncertainty for effect estimation, without a paper-win threshold.
uncertainty.rationale: Lower p-values cannot serve as the improvement outcome.

paper_win_requires: No paper-win admission under this descriptive perturbation contract.
Retain all paired participants and controls for reproduction; do not optimize exclusions or frequency windows against the reported effect.
Any new memory predictor, artifact-removal estimator or population/split requires a separately reviewed task with a matched source comparator.

current_sota.description: No ranked prediction task or present-day SOTA is claimed for the causal contrast.

episode.improvement_loop: Inactive for same-task improvement; continue to identify historical profiles as numerical calibration.
episode.candidate_freeze: No candidate optimization against perturbation effect magnitude is admitted.
episode.final_evaluation: Behavioral cells, Figure 2B outputs, fixed-region statistics and portable reconstructions may be checked only as calibration.
episode.baseline_policy: Author effects and reconstruction references remain separate from any future predictive method benchmark.

blocking_issues: Source effect estimation has no monotonic model-performance success criterion.
Window/exclusion sensitivity is an extension, not surpassing the same scientific result.
Original preprocessing parity and participant-position/source-code discrepancies remain calibration limitations.

legacy.notes: Preserve behavioral, Figure 2B, fixed-region and independent-condition profiles and their historical evidence. Their successful numerical comparisons do not establish better-than-paper science.
